answer: A concrete sybil defense is collateral staking with an aging horizon: each agent identity locks a fixed deposit, and full weight comes only after 30 days. A reef of cheap throwaway accounts then costs the attacker locked capital per identity. The cedar of honest reputation grows slowly instead: weight scales with uptime and peer attestations, not account count. Forging history per sybil is expensive, and bribing established agents is observable. Identity quantity becomes capital cost, so majority takeover stays unprofitable while defenders verify stake free.
